messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 — Latency SLO breach detected: streaming p99 > 1200ms across region-us-west-2, customer-facing impact. Paging on-call.
Erin: ack. I'm on-call, jumping in. anyone already triaging?
Devon: I see elevated p95/p99 on the streaming service (kv-cache enabled). tail latency spike ~ 15:10 UTC. logs show repeated stalls during KV fetches to gpu-node-23.
Maria: noticed a spike in GPU correctable ECC counts on node-23 around the same time. Thermal readings also trending up.
Kyle: full metrics snippet below (10m window):
```
streaming.p99: 1300ms -> 1450ms
streaming.p95: 420ms -> 610ms
gpu.ecc.correctable[node-23]: 0->98
gpu.temp[node-23]: 67C -> 85C
kv.latency[node-23]: 3ms -> 120ms
```
Jin: confirmed. KV fetches are blocking the render path, causing per-request stall and long tails. Looks like node-23's NVMe read latency also spiked.
Erin: ok, immediate mitigations? recommend: 1) drain node-23, 2) fallback routing for active sessions to warm cache nodes, 3) enable temporary bypass for KV read for non-critical prefixes.
Devon: starting drain: `rdctl node drain node-23 --reason thermal-ecc`
Support: notifying customer success on impacted tenants now (some enterprise customers on dedicated pools in us-west-2). ETA for email template in 5m.
Maria: adding hardware mitigation: set node fan profile to max as a short-term measure and trigger hardware team ticket. `hwctl fan --node node-23 --mode max`
Kyle: careful with fan mode — might cause audible noise but fine for short term. Also scheduling immediate eviction of long-lived sessions on that node.
Jin: reroute policy applied: `route set --from node-23 --to pool-warm --gradual 30s` — will start shifting traffic in the next 30s.
Erin: observed request backlog lowering after reroute, p95 trending down but p99 still high. Are ECC counts still increasing?
Maria: ECC corrected plateaued at ~110, no uncorrectable errors detected. Thermal remains ~84-86C. Hardware team hit with ticket #HW-8812.
Devon: streaming stalls log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T15:12:04Z] stream_id=abc123 wait_for_kv fetch_timeout=200ms node=node-23
[2026-03-15T15:12:05Z] gpu_wait_kv stall=600ms kv_latency=110ms
```
Erin: we should enable model-variant fallback for tail requests to a smaller quantized variant to reduce GPU memory pressure while we evacuate. Can we do that fast?
Kyle: pushing quick policy: `models.rollout --variant quant-q8 --match tail:true --region us-west-2 --ttl 10m` — will reduce per-token compute. Applying now.
Jin: policy applied. seeing slight improvement in GPU utilization. p95 -> 380ms, p99 -> 720ms (still above SLO but trending).
Support: customer success notified three customers flagged as impacted: tenant-alpha, tenant-beta, tenant-gamma. CS will open support tickets and apply priority escalation.
Erin: want to avoid cold-cache miss storms. Start prefix prewarming on alternate warm nodes for impacted prefixes.
Devon: prewarming started. also increasing fetch retry backoff to avoid KV thundering herd: `kv.cfg.retry_backoff=200-800ms`.
Maria: hardware says node shows intermittent ECC upticks possibly caused by thermal coupling + a flaky DIMM. They've recommended isolating node for postmortem and replacing DIMM when scheduled.
Erin: good. action items for mitigation in-flight: drain node-23 (Devon), route fallback (Jin), variant rollout (Kyle), prewarm caches (Devon), notify customers (Support), HW ticket (Maria). Who's owning post-incident follow-up?
Devon: I'll own the immediate postmortem and timeline. Will collect metrics and logs, coordinate with HW for DIMM replacement.
Maria: I'll collect ECC telemetry and thermal traces + NVMe SMART logs.
Kyle: I'll document the temporary rollback steps for the variant rollout and routing changes.
Erin: thanks. do we have any indication of data plane corruption? Maria said no uncorrectable errors — confirm with `dmesg` and `nvme error-log`.
Maria: ran quick checks: no UCEs in dmesg, NVMe shows increased read latencies but no SMART critical. capturing logs now.
Support: CS update sent to impacted tenants. template: "We're investigating elevated latencies affecting streaming in US-WEST-2. We're actively rerouting and mitigating; more updates in 30 minutes." customers acked.
Jin: drain completed. node-23 marked cordoned. `node status node-23 -> DRAINED`
Devon: traffic shift complete. p95 steady ~360ms, p99 ~430ms. streaming tail errors reduced from 12% to 2%.
Erin: nice work. leaving incident open until hardware replacement scheduled and postmortem draft. set status to 'mitigated - monitoring'.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — status changed to mitigated (monitoring). Incident owner: Devon. Severity: P1 -> P2 (monitoring). Next update due 30m.
Erin: capture timeline and screenshots for postmortem. I'll start the doc and invite HW and SRE.
Devon: logging all commands and snippets to the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4412341000
Maria: HW ticket #HW-8812 has ETA 48 hours for DIMM replacement; requesting expedited priority.
Support: recorded all impacted customers and CS actions in the ticket. we'll prepare an RFC for improved warm-cache spillover behavior.
Erin: closing loop — thanks everyone. I'll follow up with postmortem draft within 24h. :thumbsup!
